summary: A cardholder makes ordinary purchase transactions during a billing cycle, stays below the credit limit, receives a statement, and then pays the full statement balance on the due date. The scenario is designed to show an on-time full-payment path with no late fee and no over-limit fee, while also reflecting the issuer's purchase grace-period treatment.
assumptions: The account has no previous balance at the start of this billing cycle, so the purchase grace-period condition is satisfied under clause.6.grace_period.
Only purchase transactions occur in this scenario; there are no cash advances, balance transfers, returned payments, foreign transactions, or disputed charges.
The statement due date is 25 days after statement closing, satisfying the contract's 'not less than 25 days' grace period for purchases.
Payments are made through an approved standard method and credited on the date received.
The full statement balance is paid on the due date, which also exceeds the minimum payment required under the agreement.
Because the outstanding balance never exceeds the credit limit, no over-limit fee is triggered.
Because payment is made on or before the due date, no late payment fee or default is triggered.
